newsitem.title: UK: Jordan's prince warns of perils in Middle East.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's prince warns of perils in Middle East.

text.p: Jordan's Crown Prince El Hassan bin Talal said on Monday the Middle East peace process could unravel in the weeks ahead and stressed the importance of concluding peace negotiations.
In a speech to the Royal United Services Institute for Defence Studies, King Hussein's younger brother said the alternative to peace in the region would be long-term instability.
"The chance exists to make order out of chaos," he told an audience at the British think-tank. "The path to peace is tortuous and dangerous but it is the only path."
He said that despite lengthy negotiations the parties have failed to agree on a clear definition of the region and added that there is a need to raise the sights of the peace process.

As the prince spoke in London the Israel army reopened the campus at Hebron University on Monday after 300 students and faculty stormed the facility that has been closed since March after a wave of suicide bombings.
"The region stumbles from crisis to crisis," said the prince, adding that Jordan was uniquely placed to contribute to the longer-term situation in the Middle East.
His comments came just a week after his brother, King Hussein, voiced similar concerns about the lack of progress in the peace negotions.
